primary_claim: Opus 4.5 has a no-CoT (single forward pass) 50% reliability time horizon of 3.5 minutes on easy math problems, and this no-CoT time horizon across frontier Anthropic models has been doubling every 9 months, slower than the ~4-6 month doubling time for with-CoT SWE time horizon

effect.value: Opus 4.5: 3.5 min (with repeats), doubling every ~9 months across frontier Anthropic models

stated_future_work: Discuss and validate the no-CoT time horizon methodology with historical trends and sanity checks in a future post
Investigate time horizons on other distributions besides competition math
Investigate multi-hop out-of-context reasoning performance without CoT
limitations_stated: Human completion times are estimated by Opus 4.5 rather than actual human baselines
Fit is done only on frontier Anthropic models, excluding DeepSeek-v3
Dataset doesn't measure time horizons well below ~0.5 minutes
Evaluated only on competition math problems; time horizons may differ on other distributions
Does not allow for encoded reasoning in CoT, only single forward pass performance
Gemini results use a hacky prefill-based approach to suppress reasoning that behaves unpredictably depending on prompt template
Possible contamination in the math dataset used
quote: I find that Opus 4.5 has a no-CoT 50% reliability time horizon of 3.5 minutes and that time horizon has been doubling every 9 months.
